plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than my value, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I will bid my true value of $40 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding higher than your value risks paying more than the item is worth if you win, while bidding lower risks losing an auction you could have profitably won. With my value at $13, I should bid exactly $13 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, shading my bid provides no benefit and only risks losing a profitable auction, while overbidding risks a loss. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $17 to maximize expected profit.
